sentences.text: The petitioner is aggrieved with the action of the 4th respondent in having stopped the water supply to the petitioner as per Ext.P12.
The petitioner has set up an industry within the industrial park of the 4th respondent, for production of packaged drinking water.

The petitioner contends that the order at Ext.P12, now issued by the 4th respondent is an attempt to frustrate the smooth functioning of the industry when the earlier allegations were found to be unsubstantiated.

2. Earlier certain residents of the locality had raised allegations of misuse of ground water; when the petitioner was before this Court and a Division Bench of this Court had appointed an Advocate Commissioner who inspected the premises of the petitioner.

The Advocate Commissioner had specifically reported that there was no bore well or tube well in the business premises of the petitioner and the industry is carried on using the water, supplied by the Water Authority.
The allegation at that point was depletion of ground water; which is unfounded for reason of the petitioner not using any ground water.
Ext.P8 is the interim order passed by this Court the permitting the activity of the petitioner, which later was made absolute by judgment produced at Ext.P9.
The very same parties are now responsible for instigating the water authority to stop the supply; resulting in Ext.P12 is the argument.

The petitioner cannot validly raise such a contention,
in which none of the private parties are impleaded.

3. The learned Counsel refers to Ext.P2 and P4, which are the agreements entered into between the petitioner and the 4th respondent, wherein the 4th respondent has agreed to supply water to the consumer's premises, at the rate, fixed by the 4th respondent and the power to disconnect such connection is only on specific instances as prescribed under Clause 4 of Ext.P4.
None of these situations have arisen at this point.
It is also contented that Clause16 provides 60 days notice in writing which also has not been granted to the petitioner.
The petitioner submits that the supply has been stopped by the 4th respondent unilaterally and in violation of the agreement.

4. The learned Counsel appearing for the 4th respondent would however submit that the supply agreement was subject to the reservation as noticed in Clause18 which specifically was referred to in the impugned order.

The Water Authority having stopped the supply, the 4th respondent cannot be Varuna Aqua Products Private Limited vs State Of Kerala on 23 November, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83339984/
4 held to be responsible for the same, is the contention.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. A counter affidavit has been filed by the respondents 5 and 6.

The learned Counsel appearing for the Water Authority refers to the Kerala Water Authority (Water Supply) Regulations, 1991 (for brevity 'the regulations'), which speaks of an industrial connection, as has been defined in Clause 2(hh) which does not take in the supply of water for resale after bottling.

It is submitted that the water supplied by the Water Authority is at the rate of 14 paise per litre while the petitioner is selling the same far in excess of the price for which it is purchased, after merely packaging it.
6. Undisputed is the fact that the water supply has been stopped for reason of the water connection having been severed by the Water Authority.
The agreements speak of specific instances for disconnection of the supply and none of these instances have arisen in the above case.

But Clause18,
cannot be ignored which is extracted hereunder:-
Clause18: The water connection will be given from the water available from Kerala Water Authority (KWA).
The supply of water will be governed by the availability from KWA and KIAP will not be liable for the discontinuance in supply of water due to non availability of water from KWA.

7. The impugned order at Ext.P12 specifically speaks of the aforesaid Clause and informs the petitioner that the supply has been disconnected only for reason of the Water Authority having disconnected it.
In such circumstance, there cannot be any violation of the agreement found as against the 4th respondent.

It is an admitted fact that the petitioner does not have any agreement or contract with the Water Authority for supply of water and hence the pleading of the authority of absence of privity of contract has to be accepted.
The petitioner was using the connection made available by the Water Authority to the 4th respondent, an industrial connection, with separate meter fitted for the petitioner.
The Authority having found the operation of the petitioner of packaging and selling, water supplied by it, not one coming within the definition of an industrial purpose has severed the connection.

8. Regulation 2(hh) of the regulations has to be noticed, which is as follows:
2(hh): 'industrial connection' means the connection provided from the main to a premises to supply water for manufacturing process which includes a Motor Vehicle Service Station, Printing Press, Laundry and where water is used as part of such manufacturing process and includes usage for air conditioning, refrigeration,
washing and cleaning of the premises.
9.

The specific contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the Water Authority is that the water as supplied for an industrial connection though can be used for manufacturing process and for washing and cleaning, it cannot be permitted to be sold commercially after bottling it.
There is no manufacturing process involved in packaging of water and selling it.

It is also relevant that the Water Authority supplies water at a subsidized rate, even when it is an industrial connection and none can use the water supplied for commercial exploitation, in the same firm, which would also be Varuna Aqua Products Private Limited vs State Of Kerala on 23 November, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83339984/
5 detrimental to public interest.

sentences.text: 10. The learned Counsel for the petitioner also has a contention that the Kerala Water Supply and Sewage Water Act, 1986 (for brevity 'the Act of 1986) by Section 15A specifically confers power to manufacture market and sell packaged drinking water, mineral water etc:.

entities.text: Kerala Water Supply and Sewage Water Act, 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is very clear from a reading of Section 15A that the power conferred to manufacture, market and sell packaged drinking water, mineral water etc; is on the Water Authority and there is no power vested on the Authority to delegate such activity to a private entrepreneur.
11. A further contention raised by the petitioner based on Ext.P17 is with respect to the use permitted as a raw material.
It is the contention that the petitioner uses the water as a raw material and hence there could be no restriction caused.
Ext.P18 even according to the petitioner is only a policy document which cannot override a statutory definition.
The petitioner does not have any vested right to claim supply from the Water Authority by virtue of a statutory prescription or even a contract.
The judgment of this Court in the earlier round also cannot bind the Water Authority since it was never a party there.
The petitioner also does not have a case of any manufacturing being carried out.
12. The petitioner also has a contention with respect to another similar industry carried on at Palakkad which is evidenced by Ext.P16.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Water Authority submits that there is no connection granted anywhere in the State, except that in Palakkad and in the case of the petitioner, where water is exploited for the purpose of bottling and commercial sale.
The Managing Director has directed action against the Officers, who granted the connection in both instances is the assertion.

Considering the contentions raised on behalf of the Water Authority,
this Court is not inclined to permit the petitioner to continue exploiting the water supplied by the Water Authority for commercial sale.
The writ petition would stand dismissed.
No costs.
